sections.title: Retrieving a bag from a theatre

script.speaker: Desk clerk
script.text: You have reached the lost property desk at Harbour Theatre. I can look through the items from the weekend and arrange a time for you to check the bag.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: All right. Let’s go through the details.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: Could you confirm the performance title?

script.speaker: Desk clerk
script.text: I have your visit listed under The Orchard. The other performance in the building that evening was a concert.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: What have you put down for the seat row?

script.speaker: Desk clerk
script.text: You were in row G. That is the letter after F, so I will check the items from that area first.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: What should I write for the bag colour?

script.speaker: Desk clerk
script.text: The bag found near the aisle is navy. There was also a bright green bag, but its description is different.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: And what is the outside pocket contains a?

script.speaker: Desk clerk
script.text: There is a key in the outside pocket. I will leave it there so you can recognise the bag when you see it.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: Could you confirm the collection day?

script.speaker: Desk clerk
script.text: You can come on Tuesday. The building is closed to visitors on Monday while the next show is prepared.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: What have you put down for the collection time?

script.speaker: Desk clerk
script.text: Your collection time is 4:20 p.m. The main ticket counter opens later than that.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: What should I write for the required document?

script.speaker: Desk clerk
script.text: Bring the receipt for your theatre booking. It can be on a phone; we do not need a printed copy.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: And what is the collection entrance?

script.speaker: Desk clerk
script.text: Use the west entrance. The doors on the east side remain locked until the evening performance.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: Could you confirm the desk reference?

script.speaker: Desk clerk
script.text: Your reference is P17. That is P followed by one seven, rather than the number printed on the seat receipt.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: What have you put down for the number of days the desk holds items?

script.speaker: Desk clerk
script.text: The desk keeps items for fourteen days after they are found. Let us know if you cannot come within that period.

script.speaker: Desk clerk
script.text: Show the message at the desk when you arrive. If the item is not yours, we will check the remaining list with you.

sections.title: Following the route through a watermill

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Begin on the central cross shown on the mill site plan. North is at the top. The river is close to the buildings, so stay on the marked paths.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The wheel house is east of the junction, along the path on the right. It is the building closest to the moving water.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The grain loft is north of the junction, at the top of your plan. The path rises gently before the entrance.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The stone workshop is west of the junction. The left-hand path ends at its wide wooden door.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The tea shelter stands south of the junction. You will recognise it as the open structure at the bottom of the plan.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: We will start with a model. It shows the parts of the mechanism without having to stand next to the moving wheel.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Leave the safety gate closed until the guide reaches it. It separates visitors from the work area.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The older sacks are behind glass. The bag on the bench is a recent copy that you may touch.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The talk lasts twelve minutes. After it finishes we will have a short pause before walking back.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Look at the small jars on the workshop table. Each contains a different type of grain.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Collect the activity sheet at the exit. A volunteer will give you a pencil there as well.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: We finish at the junction, where the group can collect its bags. The paths must remain clear for the next tour.

sections.title: Organising a study of water use

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: For our design class, we are comparing two ways of collecting water from a small roof model. We need to choose the same conditions for the two trials.

script.speaker: Samir
script.text: All right. Let’s go through the details.

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Compare the volume collected. We considered measuring the colour of the water, but our project is about collection rather than water quality.

script.speaker: Samir
script.text: Keep the roof angle the same. The material of the collection channel will vary, and we will not use the same container for both samples.

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Repeating each trial will show whether the result is consistent. It is not intended to increase the water pressure or to improve the appearance of the model.

script.speaker: Samir
script.text: Chloe will make the collection channels. Samir will bring the containers and Jo will photograph the set-up.

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Samir will bring the containers. We need two of the same size so the volumes can be checked easily.

script.speaker: Samir
script.text: Jo will photograph the set-up at the start. The pictures should include the angle of the roof and the position of the channel.

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Pour from the same height in every trial. Changing it could affect how much water splashes away.

script.speaker: Samir
script.text: Leave the channel for one minute before measuring the water. That allows the last drops to run down.

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Set a separate tray under the model for splashes. That water should not be counted as collected.

script.speaker: Samir
script.text: Put the trial number next to each volume in the table. We want to keep the repetitions separate until the analysis.

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Record each test as it is done. Once we know whether the measurements are reliable, we can decide which part of the model to alter next.

sections.title: Why a repair can change a material’s behaviour

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Today we will look at a damaged strip of material and a simple repair. A successful join needs to carry a load and allow the strip to move as required.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Begin by recording the position of the tear. Take this observation before you add any new material.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: The new strip needs to cross the gap. It helps transfer force from one side to the other.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: A very stiff strip can prevent the repaired area from bending smoothly. Check the flexibility as well as whether it stays attached.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Use a clip to keep the pieces in place while the join sets. Remove the clip before testing the strip.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Draw an arrow for the expected pull. This keeps the direction of the test clear when you compare several samples.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Add the small weights one at a time. This gives you a record of when the join begins to move.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Record the load when you first see movement. Complete failure is not the only outcome worth noting.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Use a second strip with no repair for comparison. Its behaviour will help you interpret what changed in the first strip.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Inspect the edge of the new strip after loading. Damage can start there before the centre shows a change.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Take one image before and one after the test. Use the same distance so the positions can be compared directly.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: The strongest repair in one direction may not be the best for another use. Your report should describe how the strip was supported and what it needed to do.
